name: Test Driven Development Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday test driven development work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical test driven development tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday test driven development work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical test driven development tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to test driven development (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. Document any non-obvious test driven development decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. State assumptions about test driven development explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. When test driven development guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen test driven development approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Keep test driven development changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. When multiple test driven development strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
8. Validate test driven development outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of test driven development correctness.
- Avoid introducing new test driven development abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated test driven development concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for test driven development, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
